bib.title: Advancing Transformer Architecture in Long-Context Large Language Models: A Comprehensive Survey

question: How can the Transformer architecture be modified, across pretraining, finetuning, inference and pre/postprocessing, so LLMs handle long-context input and output effectively and efficiently?
contributions: A holistic taxonomy of Transformer-architecture methods for long-context LLMs across pretraining, fine-tuning, inference and pre/postprocessing
A review of evaluation necessities (datasets, metrics, baselines) and optimization toolkits (libraries, frameworks, compilers)

limits: Survey of literature to ~Jan 2024; no new experiments except the authors say they ran 'elementary experiments' on ReRoPE (not reported) and re-implemented a Flash-Attention ReRoPE kernel in Triton
Quantitative figures are quoted from other papers and not re-verified
Discussion concedes efficient attention trades attention precision for compute and long-term memory mechanisms add overhead and may degrade over time
Authors concede positional-embedding extensions rely on simplified observations and heuristic adjustments, lacking theory
Authors note metrics diverge from human judgment and LLM judges (GPT4) are costly
Dataset, baseline and toolkit tables (Apps A-D) are snapshots; model context lengths (e.g. GPT4-Turbo 128k, Claude2 100k) have dated
practices: Choose among five method classes by target module: efficient attention (Sec 3), long-term memory (Sec 4), extrapolative PEs (Sec 5), context processing (Sec 6), miscellaneous (Sec 7)
For off-the-shelf LLMs without retraining, use context processing (selection, aggregation, compression) at the cost of multiple calls and possibly less precise answers (Sec 6)
For RoPE models, extend context with scaling (PI, NTK-aware, Dynamic-NTK, YaRN) or truncation (ReRoPE) with minimal or no finetuning (Sec 5.3)
Use IO-aware exact attention (FlashAttention, Paged Attention) when precision cannot be traded for speed (Sec 3.5)
Use external memory banks with retrieval (RAG) to decouple memory from the model and avoid retraining and memory staleness (Sec 4.2)
Use GQA/MQA and quantization to reduce KV cache and weight memory (Sec 7)
Combine parallelism strategies (DP, TP, PP, SP, EP; 3D/4D) to scale model size and sequence length (Sec 7)

terms.definition: the upper bound on sequence length for any training sample in a batch, commonly set as 1K, 2K, or 4K
a list of tensors that stores the k, v embeddings for all previous tokens in the attention layer for each block
the model is trained on short sequences but tested on longer ones during inference
strong attention towards initial tokens even if they are not semantically important; keeping their KV recovers sliding-window performance
the boundary of RoPE dimensions that perceive complete periodic information during training
linear scaling of each position number from n to n/kappa, extending the length boundary by kappa times
combines high-frequency extrapolation and low-frequency interpolation by scaling beta by c_kappa = kappa^(2/(d-2))
rectified truncation: no scaling inside a local window w, constant position w beyond it (kappa to infinity)
exact attention computed with attention to GPU HBM/SRAM traffic via tiling and online softmax
recurrence-based cache of detached hidden states from previous segments prepended to the current segment
retrieval-augmented storage of segmented embedding vectors outside the model, retrieved into in-context working memory
